events.name: Scissor Street
events.intro: One street, two salons. On the left, a quiet shop with a brush in the window. On the right, mirrors, feathers, a queue round the corner, and a sign: SALON ROCKET: BEAUTY IS PAIN (YOURS). Suzie, in the quiet one: "They paint them. Glitter in the fur. It looks very fine, and it itches, and the Pokémon can't tell you it itches. I only do what they'd ask for, if they could ask." From across the road, a stylist with remarkable hair: "Dated! Health is over, darling! It's all about the look!"

success.text: She works with her hands, and talks to it, and stops when it flinches. "There. That's where it was sore. You've been leading with that shoulder." It takes no node.
The queue on the right doesn't move. Nobody in it looks happy, including the Pokémon.

events.name: Scissor Street: The Style-Off
events.intro: The loud salon challenges anything she's groomed.

success.text: Their Pokémon are in ribbons and paint, slow and scratching. The crowd, slowly noticing: "...Why's that Ekans miserable? Mine never looks like that. Oh. Mine never looks like anything."
Suzie smiles at the brush in her hand.
They start the motto. They're wearing curlers. It doesn't land.

events.name: Scissor Street: The Style-Off
events.intro: Curlers, a motto, and a challenge.

success.text: Ribbons, paint, and an itch.
Suzie smiles at the brush in her hand.

events.name: Scissor Street: The Queue Crosses
events.intro: The queue crosses the road.

success.text: Suzie asks you to look after her Vulpix for a while: "She wants to see somewhere I can't take her. Bring her back if she asks. She won't ask."

effects.text: Won a style-off on Scissor Street with a Pokémon that only wanted brushing.

events.name: The Diner

remembers.notice: He looks at your coins, and nods, and orders a fresh coffee.

events.intro: A counter. One man, one cold coffee, one empty leather case on the stool beside him. Mr. Desmond Skeffington: "Take it. The case. I can't throw it away; I'd fish it out. If you've got it, I'd have to ask for it back, and I'd be too ashamed. That's the only lock I've got left."

success.text: The Coin Case. And his three tips, whether asked or not: "The machines by the door are loose. So people outside can hear them paying." "Never play the one somebody's just left. It's cold." "Third from the end, back row. I watched it all week. I never sat at it. I don't know why." Only one of those is true; you'll find out which by trying.
"All of what I had, and some of what I didn't."
"There is. That's why I'm in here and not in there."

events.name: The Diner
events.intro: The case, on the stool.

success.text: The Coin Case. And his three tips, whether asked or not: "The machines by the door are loose. So people outside can hear them paying." "Never play the one somebody's just left. It's cold." "Third from the end, back row. I watched it all week. I never sat at it. I don't know why." Only one of those is true; you'll find out which by trying.
He doesn't look at it after you go. He doesn't look at anything.

events.name: The Poster
events.intro: A poster of a Clefairy on the back wall. A man in black standing with his back flat against it. The Grunt: "I'm admiring the machines." He's facing away from them. "From here. I admire them from here. It's the best angle."

success.text: Four minutes. He looks at his watch. He goes for a sandwich. You go in one room further than anyone was meant to.
He moves, eventually, under protest.

choices.label: Reach past him and press it.

success.text: The wall slides. You're going in early.
"It's a perfectly ordinary poster! There's nothing behind it! Why would you say 'behind'? I didn't say 'behind'!"

events.name: The Poster
events.intro: He is pressed very flat against the Clefairy.

success.text: Four minutes. He looks at his watch. He goes for a sandwich. You go in one room further than anyone was meant to.

choices.label: Reach past him and press it.

success.text: The wall slides. You're going in early.

events.name: The Developers' Room
events.intro: A small office. Four desks. Four people who look as if they've been here since before the building. The one who draws: "I did the pictures. All of them. The Pidgey took a week. Nobody notices the Pidgey." The one who writes: "I wrote what people say. I'm sorry about some of it. It was late." The one who programs: "If something odd happened to you out there, that was me. It wasn't meant to. I've left it in. I've grown fond of it." The fourth, not looking up: "..." The one who writes: "We don't know what he does. He was here when we came." They ask how many kinds you've met.

success.text: A hand-signed Diploma (four signatures, one of them a dot), and a Porygon "left over." The fourth, as you leave, for the only time: "It was worth doing. Tell them."

effects.text: Got a diploma from the people who drew the Pidgey: four signatures, one of them a dot.

success.text: A PP Up. The fourth, as you leave, for the only time: "It was worth doing. Tell them."
A Rare Candy. "Go and meet more. We made a lot." The fourth, as you leave, for the only time: "It was worth doing. Tell them."

events.name: The Bridge Run
events.intro: A Pokémon Center with the phone ringing. A nurse with a parcel and no way to send it. The nurse: "There's a Shellder at Sunnytown that won't last the night without this. The road's eight hours. The bridge is one, and it isn't finished, and there's a storm due, and there are people on it who don't let anyone by." Without a bike of your own, she lends you hers. Twelve turns, three parts.

success.text: The bag goes on your back. The rain starts on the first pedal stroke.
She nods, and keeps dialling.

events.name: The Bridge Run: The Gang
events.intro: Bikers across the bridge's mouth. Chopper: "Toll's a battle. Two if you're in a hurry."

success.text: You pick moves while steering.
Off the road, through a hedge, back on. It costs time.

events.name: The Bridge Run: The Reason
events.intro: Tyra: "What's in the bag?"

success.text: They look at each other. They kick their stands up. "Sunnytown. My nan's in Sunnytown. Move, you lot. Make a lane." With the escort: twenty headlamps in the rain, and you in the middle of them.
The second battle, and no escort.

events.name: The Bridge Run: The Drawbridge
events.intro: It's going up.

success.text: The escort holds it, and you go over.
You clear the gap with a foot to spare.

failure.text: You land short and walk the last bit with the bike on your shoulder.

events.name: The Bridge Run: Sunnytown
events.intro: A child in pyjamas at the Center door, waiting.

success.text: The gang's patch: bikers on the Cycling Road leave you be. From the Shellder's trainer, a child in pyjamas: a bundle of Sitrus Berries.

effects.text: Rode a parcel over an unfinished bridge in a storm, inside twenty headlamps.

success.text: It's delivered anyway. The Shellder's poorly, and pulls through. The patch only. Chopper, after: "We got it there. You didn't. Don't feel bad. Feel a bit bad."

events.name: The Greenhouse Fire

remembers.notice: It's the trio's dropped lamp. They're on the bucket chain, at the back, in the gardener scarves, saying nothing.

events.intro: Smoke over the rooftops. Glass breaking, a pane at a time. The perfume greenhouse. Staff with buckets. Erika, held back by two of her own gardeners, not shouting: saying one thing, over and over, quietly. "She won't leave. She thinks it's hers to mind. She's old. She won't leave." Six turns. Three rooms deep.

success.text: In.

events.name: The Greenhouse Fire: The First Room
events.intro: Smoke, and the heat coming off the glass.

success.text: The room's fire goes out with a hiss.
Two turns, and your lead takes a burn.

events.name: The Greenhouse Fire: The Second Room
events.intro: Smoke, and the heat coming off the glass.

success.text: The room's fire goes out with a hiss.
Two turns, and your lead takes a burn.

events.name: The Greenhouse Fire: The Last Room
events.intro: An old Gloom, in the middle of the oldest bed, with its leaves over the seedlings. A Poison or Grass type is immune to the smell; anything else is stunned a turn, because she's frightened, and it shows.

success.text: You carry her.
She follows at once.

choices.label: "It's all right. You've minded it. Come on."

success.text: She looks at you a long time, and comes.

events.name: The Greenhouse Fire: Out
events.intro: The door, and air.

success.text: A Leaf Stone. Free perfume. A friend in Celadon for the rest of the run. Erika: "I once shut my door on somebody who said she smelled. I think about that. She'd have gone in after them, too."

effects.text: Carried an old Gloom out of Erika's burning greenhouse.

success.text: The firefighters get her out a minute later, singed and cross. Erika thanks you for trying.

events.name: The Unstable Eevee
events.intro: Behind the prize counter, a door marked STOCK. From behind it, a sound that keeps changing: a splash, a crackle, a hiss. A cage. Inside, something blue with a fin. A guard drops his keys. It's yellow, and every hair's on end. You step forward. It's red. Between each, for half a second, it's small and brown, and it looks at you. The guard: "Don't startle it! It does a different one every time. The buyers love it. Three for the price of one."

success.text: He fights to keep the cage shut.
The sound goes on changing behind the door.

events.name: The Unstable Eevee: The Cage

remembers.notice: Later, the Eeveelution Brothers go quiet when they hear. Mikey: "Somebody made it choose? All of them?" Pyro puts his stone in his pocket.

events.intro: The cage is open. It's in the far corner, changing, changing. It isn't a Shadow Pokémon, and it's never forced to change.

success.text: It settles into that form for good, and joins. It breathes out, as if it's been holding it for months.
It settles into that form for good, and joins. It breathes out, as if it's been holding it for months.
It settles into that form for good, and joins. It breathes out, as if it's been holding it for months.

choices.label: "No stone. Take as long as you need."

success.text: It joins as an Eevee. It bonds slower, and it's worth it.

effects.text: Waited for a frightened Eevee to stop changing, and let it stay an Eevee.

events.name: The Big P Ranch
events.intro: Open grassland. A herd of Tauros moving like weather. A girl on a Ponyta, turning them with a whistle. Lara: "Race is tomorrow. The ranch that wins runs the reserve. We've won nine years." That night: a spooked herd, a fall. Her arm's in a sling by morning. "It's not broken. It's not good. She won't take anyone but me. She burns them. You could try. You'd need to mean it." You reach for the mane. It's hot. It isn't hot enough to stop you, quite. The Ponyta's watching to see what you'll do about that.

success.text: It costs your pride and a blister; nobody's harmed.

choices.label: "Take my hand away. Wait. Try again."

success.text: The second time, it lets you.
You ask. It thinks about it. It lowers its head.

events.name: The Big P Ranch: The Hills
events.intro: Slow, careful. A rival rider on a Dodrio, Dario, who's very sure of himself, and whose friends have been at the fences.

choices.label: Let her run her own race.

success.text: Careful. She notices you didn't push.

choices.label: Let her run her own race.

success.text: She does, carefully.
Faster, for one stride. She feels you ask, and she goes, and something between you goes the other way a little.

events.name: The Big P Ranch: The River
events.intro: Stepping stones. Ponyta hates water.

choices.label: Let her run her own race.

success.text: She jumps without being asked.

choices.label: Let her run her own race.

success.text: She does, carefully.
Faster, for one stride. She feels you ask, and she goes, and something between you goes the other way a little.

events.name: The Big P Ranch: The Sprint
events.intro: Flat out against the Dodrio.

choices.label: Let her run her own race.

success.text: The flames go white.

choices.label: Let her run her own race.

success.text: She does, carefully.
Faster, for one stride. She feels you ask, and she goes, and something between you goes the other way a little.

events.name: The Big P Ranch: The Line
events.intro: The line.

success.text: The line. The Ponyta's gone over it as something taller. It's evolved in the last stride. Lara: "She never did that for me. ...No. She did it for her. You just didn't get in the way. That's the hard part." One of this year's foals: a Ponyta. And Charcoal.

effects.text: Won the Big P race on a Ponyta that wouldn't take anyone, by not getting in her way.

success.text: The ranch is kept anyway: a neighbour's loan. The foal's still offered. "You rode her kind. That's what I'm paying for."

events.name: The Child of the Herd
events.intro: The long grass parts. Something small, fast and furious comes out of it, and it isn't a Pokémon. A boy of six or seven, in a fur wrap, with a boomerang. He throws it at your feet. It comes back to him. "Kanga! Kanga-kanga! Go!" Behind him, a Kangaskhan, very large, entirely calm. Overhead, as every evening for five years: a helicopter, going round. At the gate, a man and a woman in expensive, worn-out clothes. The mother: "He fell out. He was three. We've flown over this place every day since. We see him, sometimes. He looks well. That's what I can't get past."

choices.label: Stay the night near the herd.

success.text: That night: poachers. A lorry, nets, a tranquilliser rig. A dart, a Kangaskhan going down slowly, the boy standing over her with the boomerang.
The helicopter goes round again.

events.name: The Child of the Herd: Poachers
events.intro: You fight beside a Kangaskhan you don't command; it does what's needed.

success.text: The Kangaskhan takes the left; you take the right.

events.name: The Child of the Herd: Morning
events.intro: The helicopter's landed. The father's walking toward the herd with his hands open. The boy looks at him, and at the Kangaskhan, and back.

success.text: The boy, the only words he's got: "...Mama. Papa." And then, pointing at the herd: "Mama." The mother, after a while: "Well. We'd better stay, then. Hadn't we."

effects.text: Stood with a Kangaskhan and a boy against poachers, and watched a family decide to stay.

events.name: The Lake Nobody Fishes
events.intro: A lake with no ripples. A hut. An old warden on a chair, facing the water, with a rod across his knees that's got no line on it. Kaiser: "There's nothing in it. I've guarded the nothing for thirty years. People used to come with nets for the nothing. Whole town came. They drained half of it looking. So: there's nothing in it. You understand me."

success.text: He watches you walk off. He calls you back. At dusk, he shows you: the lake's surface, and under it, something long, turning over in its sleep. A Dragon Scale, from the shore. A Dragonair Sighting.

effects.text: Was shown the nothing in the lake nobody fishes.

choices.label: "Then you won't mind if I fish." (10% a Dratini)

success.text: A long blue shape takes the line. He doesn't watch.

failure.text: "Told you. Nothing in it." He isn't triumphant. He'd hoped better of you.

success.text: "Long. Blue. It looked at me once. I was a young fool with a net. I put the net down. I've not picked up one since."

events.name: The Lake Nobody Fishes
events.intro: The rod with no line, across his knees.

success.text: He watches you walk off. He calls you back. At dusk, he shows you: the lake's surface, and under it, something long, turning over in its sleep. A Dragon Scale, from the shore. A Dragonair Sighting.

effects.text: Was shown the nothing in the lake nobody fishes.

choices.label: "Then you won't mind if I fish." (10% a Dratini)

success.text: A long blue shape takes the line. He doesn't watch.

failure.text: "Told you. Nothing in it." He isn't triumphant. He'd hoped better of you.

events.name: The Rod Brothers and the Move Deleter
events.intro: Two doors. On one, a fish. On the other, an eraser. Mr. Barnabus Sprat, the Fishing Guru: "Do you like fishing?"

success.text: "Good! Have a rod. My brother in Vermilion gives them to people who can't. I give them to people who want to. Mine's the higher standard."
"That's not what I asked. I asked if you like it. Sitting there. Not catching."
He looks at you as if you'd said you didn't like breathing.
"Sit it down there. Which one's it tired of carrying?"

events.name: The Fishing Guru
events.intro: "Do you like it?"

success.text: "Then have a rod."
"Honest. Next door, then."

events.name: The Move Deleter
events.intro: The Move Deleter: "Sit it down there. Which one's it tired of carrying?" He can also help a Pokémon forget a Shadow move it no longer wants, at no cost.

success.text: He doesn't ask why. He puts a hand on its head, and waits, and the Pokémon's shoulders come down. "There. It didn't want that one. Somebody put it there."
He puts a hand on its head, and waits. "There." It looks lighter.
"Come back when it's tired."

events.name: The Bird Keepers' Maze: Wilton
events.intro: Wilton: "They're not lost. You're lost. They know exactly where they are."

success.text: Wilton's bird comes down off the fence.

events.name: The Bird Keepers' Maze: Edwina
events.intro: Edwina: "Mine only flies left. We've made a life of it."

success.text: Edwina's bird comes down off the fence.

events.name: The Bird Keepers' Maze: Chester
events.intro: Chester: "Don't look down. I say that to everyone. They all look down."

success.text: Chester's bird comes down off the fence.

events.name: The Bird Keepers' Maze: Roland
events.intro: Roland: "I whistle, it comes. I don't whistle, it also comes. I've stopped whistling."

success.text: Roland's bird comes down off the fence.

events.name: The Bird Keepers' Maze: Old Jacob
events.intro: Old Jacob: "Forty years on this cliff. Never been up. They go up. I hold the lunch."

success.text: Old Jacob's bird comes down off the fence.

events.name: The Bird Keepers' Maze
events.intro: A cliff road fenced into a maze. At every corner, somebody with a bird on their arm and a whistle round their neck. A sign at the gate shows both ways: Short, two battles, coins. Long, five battles: a Sharp Beak, a hidden TM, and a Doduo.

success.text: Two keepers, two birds.
Five corners, five whistles.
The birds watch you go the long way round the outside.

events.name: The Bird Keepers' Maze: The Way Out
events.intro: A Doduo that's been in the maze since it was hatched, walking the long way. It follows you out, both heads arguing about the turnings.

success.text: It joins of its own accord.

effects.text: Walked the long way through the Bird Keepers' Maze, and came out with a Doduo.

events.name: The Weakest Paras
events.intro: A herbalist's shop. A shelf of empty jars labelled MIRACLE: AWAITING INGREDIENT. Cassandra: "The medicine wants the big mushroom. A Parasect's. Mine's a Paras. It needs to evolve. It needs to win to do that, and it's never won anything. It lost to a Caterpie. The Caterpie apologised." The Paras is behind her ankle. It waves a claw, and falls over. The task: lose convincingly. A disobedient Pokémon may hit for real; you're told before, and may bench it.

success.text: Its Confidence starts at nothing.
The Paras waves. It falls over.

events.name: The Weakest Paras: Turn One
events.intro: It scratches. It wouldn't dent a leaf. Each of your moves is marked Safe or Too strong.

success.text: Your lead swings wide, very obviously. The Paras looks thrilled.
Your lead reels. The Paras stands taller.
A tap. It holds.
Too strong. The Paras faints. She thanks you anyway. She'll follow you, hopefully, to the next rest.

events.name: The Weakest Paras: Turn Two
events.intro: It scratches. It wouldn't dent a leaf. Each of your moves is marked Safe or Too strong.

success.text: Your lead swings wide, very obviously. The Paras looks thrilled.
Your lead reels. The Paras stands taller.
A tap. It holds.
Too strong. The Paras faints. She thanks you anyway. She'll follow you, hopefully, to the next rest.

events.name: The Weakest Paras: The Last Hit
events.intro: Its Confidence is full. It has to land the last hit.

success.text: Your lead takes a Scratch that wouldn't dent a leaf, staggers three steps, looks at you to check it's doing it right, and keels over with one leg in the air. The Paras stares at its own claw. It's glowing before it's finished staring. The Miracle Potion: a full heal and cure, for one Pokémon, out of battle.

effects.text: Lost, very convincingly, to the weakest Paras in Fuchsia.

events.name: The Weakest Paras: Again
events.intro: Cassandra, at the rest stop, holding the Paras up hopefully.

success.text: Again.
She waits. She's good at waiting.

events.name: The Carnival
events.intro: A carnival with nobody at it. One tent has a show on. The audience is you. Melvin the Magnificent: "And now! From this ordinary hat! A—" It's a sprinkler. It goes off. It puts out his own candles. "...It was that or the doves. The doves left." His one Exeggcute tries to help. It hypnotises your lead by accident, and looks mortified. That night: thirty Exeggutor, in step, eyes blank, marching at the carnival's fuel store. Melvin: "They'll stop when I say! Stop. ...They'll stop when it says. Tell them. ...It can't. It's hypnotised itself." Four turns.

success.text: They're startled awake. Two turns. The carnival's saved. He gives you his Exeggcute: "It deserves a better act than mine." A Miracle Seed. Melvin: "I'll do children's parties. They like the sprinkler."

effects.text: Turned thirty marching Exeggutor away from the carnival's fuel store.

success.text: The organ, at full stops. Three turns. Just. The carnival's saved. He gives you his Exeggcute: "It deserves a better act than mine." A Miracle Seed. Melvin: "I'll do children's parties. They like the sprinkler."

effects.text: Turned thirty marching Exeggutor away from the carnival's fuel store.

choices.label: "You wanted an audience. Look at what you've got instead."

success.text: He walks out in front of them, takes off the hat, and bows to nobody. The Exeggcute sees him do it, and blinks. One turn. The carnival's saved. He gives you his Exeggcute: "It deserves a better act than mine." A Miracle Seed. Melvin: "I'll do children's parties. They like the sprinkler."

effects.text: Turned thirty marching Exeggutor away from the carnival's fuel store.

events.name: Mr. Psychic
events.intro: A house with the door already open. Mr. Psychic: "...Wait. Don't say a word. You wanted this." He hands over a TM. It's Psychic. He goes on looking at you. A little longer than is comfortable. Then a little longer than that. "The building with the fountain has more floors than it admits to."

success.text: "Because you were about to ask." He seems sorry about it.
"You're welcome. You'll be back. No, you won't. Good."
"You're welcome. ...Yes, and that. No. I won't tell you how that ends. I like you."

events.name: The House of Imitation
events.intro: A small theatre. CLOSED on the door, and under it, older, THE HOUSE OF IMITATION: SHE CAN BE ANYONE! Duplica, on the edge of the stage, in half a costume: "It can do everything. The shape, the size, the moves. Watch." Her Ditto becomes your lead. It's perfect. Then it turns round. Two dots and a line. "And they laugh. Right at the sad bit. So we stopped. It thinks it's its fault. It isn't. I don't know how to tell it that in a way it'd believe."

success.text: The Ditto copies your lead. Dot eyes.
She sits on the edge of it a while longer.

events.name: The House of Imitation
events.intro: Dot eyes.

success.text: It holds a little longer.
Attacking's allowed. It wins the battle and ends the event with nothing; you were told on the first turn.

events.name: The House of Imitation
events.intro: The eyes are the right colour.

success.text: It holds a little longer.
Attacking's allowed. It wins the battle and ends the event with nothing; you were told on the first turn.

events.name: The House of Imitation
events.intro: The right shape, held for a few seconds.

success.text: It holds a little longer.
Attacking's allowed. It wins the battle and ends the event with nothing; you were told on the first turn.

events.name: The House of Imitation: Complete
events.intro: Complete. Your lead looks at it, and can't tell either. Duplica's standing up. She hasn't breathed.

success.text: "...It was never that it couldn't. It was that it was watching their faces." She reopens. Front-row seats. And a second Ditto she's been training.

effects.text: Watched a Ditto get the face right, in the front row, at the House of Imitation.

events.name: The Admissions Exam
events.intro: A hall of desks. A clock. An instructor who's failed every candidate this year and takes no pleasure in it. Mr. Percival Wickham: "Pencils down means down. Nobody passes. I tell them that at the start, and they sit it anyway. I find that either very stupid or the entire point." Six questions.

success.text: Pencils up.
"Most do. The honest ones."

events.name: The Admissions Exam: The Trick Question
events.intro: "True or false: a Pokémon that's lost can't have been well trained."

success.text: Marked wrong.
Marked wrong.

choices.label: In the margin: "It depends on what it learned."

success.text: The only one he ticks.

events.name: The Admissions Exam: The Practical
events.intro: Three Pokémon you've never used, against his three. Each has a quirk on its card: "Won't use its strongest move unless thanked first."

success.text: His three, carefully chosen.

events.name: The Admissions Exam: Results
events.intro: He checks the paper twice.

success.text: A certificate. A bundle of candy. "First this year. Don't let it go to your head. It's already gone to mine."

effects.text: Passed the Admissions Exam: the first this year.

success.text: He goes through every wrong answer, and why.

events.name: The Admissions Exam: Fail
events.intro: He goes through every wrong answer, and why. Each one sticks.

success.text: It's the best lesson you've had in Kanto.

events.name: The Teleport Girl
events.intro: Winnie: "Where to? He's been everywhere you've been. He just hasn't been awake for any of it." The Abra on her shoulder is asleep. It stays asleep. Only shops; no events are replayed, and nothing's skipped. It takes no node.

success.text: Rocks, and a Hard Stone. On return: the Abra hasn't moved. There's a souvenir sticker on its forehead. Winnie: "He does that. I don't know when."
Bait, and a Mystic Water. On return: the Abra hasn't moved. There's a souvenir sticker on its forehead. Winnie: "He does that. I don't know when."
Seven floors, and a Great Ball or two. On return: the Abra hasn't moved. There's a souvenir sticker on its forehead. Winnie: "He does that. I don't know when."
The Abra sleeps on.

events.name: The Seam
events.intro: The road into the city, and then the road stops being where it is. The air's got a shimmer on it, like heat, in the cold. Your hand goes flat against nothing. Walking the edge: a place where the light bends at a corner. Behind it, a Mr. Mime, both hands up, shaking with the effort. Beside it, a scientist asleep in a folding chair with a clipboard on his chest. The Mr. Mime sees you. It doesn't lower its hands. Its eyes say: I can't.

success.text: You learn what an anchor looks like. In the climax, you'll know them on sight. The wall thins enough to pass.
He wakes swinging.

choices.label: Mime a door, and knock on it.

success.text: The Mr. Mime laughs, despite everything. The wall flickers. It's a small thing. It remembers it.

events.name: Pidgey Post
events.intro: A post office with forty Pidgey asleep on every surface, heads under wings. The postmaster, Mrs. Zenobia Finnegan: "The roads are shut, so it all goes by wing, and there's only so much wing. Three letters. You're going that way regardless. I can pay in gratitude, and the gratitude of strangers, which is better."

success.text: Three envelopes, warm from a Pidgey.
Forty Pidgey go on sleeping.

events.name: Pidgey Post: Letter 1
events.intro: An old man.

success.text: "'I'm sorry it's been so long. I didn't know how to start, so I've started.' ...Forty years. He's started." A Berry.

events.name: Pidgey Post: Letter 2
events.intro: A shopkeeper.

success.text: "'The cheque's in the post.' It is the post. There's no cheque." A tip, out of spite.

events.name: Pidgey Post: Letter 3
events.intro: A child.

success.text: "It's from my Pidgey. It's just a footprint. It's the right footprint." A rumour about the road ahead.

events.name: Pidgey Post: All Three
events.intro: The postmaster's own Pidgeotto lands on your shoulder.

success.text: It offers to carry one message for you, anywhere in Kanto: help will reach you a node early, once.

effects.text: Delivered all three Pidgey Post letters.

events.name: The Riddle Inn
events.intro: Every hotel has a sign: FULL. Tourists with cameras. A souvenir stall selling volcano-shaped hats. A bald man in a wig that's facing slightly the wrong way: "A room? There's one. Answer three, and it's free. My Gym's— I mean: my inn's where you put firefighters. What's my inn?" Behind him, a notice board: a map, with one building circled, and a note: "ANSWERS, IN CASE I FORGET."

success.text: He clears his throat.
All three answers, circled.
The stars are very good from the beach.

events.name: The Riddle Inn: The Night
events.intro: He counts on his fingers.

success.text: A free night: a full rest. TM Fire Blast, "left by a previous guest." "He was a hot-headed man. Bald. Very handsome."
A room over the kitchen. Half a rest. The wig's fallen off by breakfast, and nobody mentions it.

events.name: The Sleeper on the Beach

remembers.notice: In the background, on a rock with its marker pen: the Jigglypuff from the road. It has seen you.

addChoices.label: Sit down in front of the Jigglypuff. Stay awake this time.

success.text: It clears its throat, very slowly, watching you.

events.intro: A sandbar. Forty Squirtle and Wartortle, asleep in heaps. In the middle, a Blastoise on its back, snoring out of one cannon. The other cannon's blocked by something round and pink. A Wartortle, the only one awake, pulls at your sleeve. It points. It mimes: singing. Then: falling over. From inside the cannon, muffled, a song. Getting close puts things to sleep.

success.text: It walks up and pulls. Done. Pop. A Jigglypuff, furious, with a marker pen. It looks at forty sleeping faces. It's the best day of its life. The Blastoise wakes, with a moustache drawn on.

One step nearer each time, and a turn asleep on the sand each time. On the third, it's close enough. Pop. A Jigglypuff, furious, with a marker pen. It looks at forty sleeping faces. It's the best day of its life. The Blastoise wakes, with a moustache drawn on.

success.text: It works. Your lead is very impressed. Pop. A Jigglypuff, furious, with a marker pen. It looks at forty sleeping faces. It's the best day of its life. The Blastoise wakes, with a moustache drawn on.

events.name: The Sleeper on the Beach: Awake
events.intro: The Blastoise sits up, and forty Squirtle and Wartortle wake round it.

success.text: A Wartortle from the island asks to come.

effects.text: Pulled a Jigglypuff out of a Blastoise's cannon.

success.text: The Wartortle that was awake has sunglasses in its shell. It puts them on.

events.name: The Backlog
events.intro: Dr. Yarrow: "I had four assistants. One left for the sea, two for the volcano, and one I think I may have revived by mistake. So there's a queue." A shelf. Three fossils, each with a paper tag: "UNCLAIMED." "Their finders never came back. I can wake them. I can't keep them. I've a flat. If you'd give one a home, I'll do it now."

success.text: He does it now. It wakes to a face it doesn't know, and decides it'll do.

effects.text: Gave an unclaimed fossil a home, from the Cinnabar Lab's shelf.

success.text: "No idea. Could be anything. That's the charm. That's also the risk."
The shelf waits.

events.name: The Trade Wing
events.intro: Three researchers; each wants one common Pokémon and offers one uncommon one. The Honest Trade Card is shown for each. A traded Pokémon arrives with its nickname and its item.

choices.label: Dr. Lettice Larkspur: a Raticate for "Doris".

success.text: A Electrode called "Doris", holding a magnet.

choices.label: Mr. Erasmus Plumb: a Venonat for "Crinkles".

success.text: A Tangela called "Crinkles", holding a miracle seed. Mr. Plumb: "He's called Crinkles. You can't change it. Well. You can. He'll know."

choices.label: Miss Millicent Roe: a Ponyta for "Seelor".

success.text: A Seel called "Seelor", holding a mystic water.
The researchers go back to their notes.

events.name: The Big Wave
events.intro: A beach on the Seafoam side. A rock offshore with two flags on it. An old man waxing a board, and a Pikachu with blue eyes standing at the waterline with its ears up. Victor: "She feels them. Before they stand up. She's been twitchy since Tuesday. Twenty years ago, a fellow put that first flag there. Forty years ago, the fellow who taught him. I've been out every big day since, and come back on my face." You ride it with one of your own Pokémon as the board.

success.text: Small waves first. Learn to lean.
The Pikachu calls every rise a beat early. Nobody goes out.

events.name: The Big Wave: Set One
events.intro: Small waves. Learn to lean.

choices.label: Ride it (a Water type as the board).

success.text: A Water type forgives one mistake.
You stay up.

failure.text: You're fished out by the collar. "There's always another wave." This run, there isn't.

events.name: The Big Wave: The Wave
events.intro: The sea goes back. A long way back. Then it stands up. The blue-eyed Pikachu rides on the nose and calls each rise a beat early, if you listen.

events.name: The Big Wave: The Flag
events.intro: The top. The whole island's below. The rock, and the two flags, coming up fast.

success.text: Victor plants your flag on the rock beside the two others. He does it himself; he's waded out. "Wasn't ever going to be mine. I worked that out about ten years back. I just wanted to see who."

effects.text: Rode the twenty-year wave, and Victor planted the flag.

events.name: The Vial

remembers.notice: It's the innkeeper, without the wig. He doesn't do a riddle. Your lead notices before you do.
The handwriting on the label is the handwriting on page 3 of the Mansion diary.

events.intro: The lip of the crater road. An old man sitting on the wall, with one sleeve rolled down in the heat. "You're going back across. I'm not. They watch the boats for me. Would you carry something? It's small. It's the heaviest thing I own." A sealed vial. Something in it that moves toward his hand when he holds it. "I made a thing for them, once. I was clever, and I was flattered, and I didn't ask what for. This is a piece of what I put in. It's the only thing it still answers to."

success.text: It's warm. It leans toward him as you walk away.

effects.text: Carried a sealed vial for an old man who couldn't take the boat.

success.text: "Something that asks questions. I'd have liked it, if I'd met it another way."

effects.text: Carried a sealed vial for an old man who couldn't take the boat.

success.text: "Because one day somebody will need it to listen. I'd rather that was possible."

effects.text: Carried a sealed vial for an old man who couldn't take the boat.

events.name: The Torch
events.intro: A runner, bent double at the roadside, holding a lit torch at arm's length as if it might notice she's stopped. "It's from the bird's own fire. It's gone hand to hand from the mountain. My handover's not here. It can't stop. Take it. To the next marker. Don't let it go out, and don't let it think you're frightened." The trio want it. Jessie: "It's a priceless relic!" James: "It's a very good lighter." Meowth: "The boss likes a candle. Look, we want it. Stop askin' why."

success.text: One battle, with the torch in one hand. The flame leans the way the battle's going.
She keeps running. You keep up for a mile. The trio don't try it with two of you.

events.name: The Torch: The Marker
events.intro: The next marker, and the next runner, hands out.

success.text: Delivered. A charm on a cord, still warm from the handle: Fire moves burn a little brighter.

effects.text: Carried the bird's fire one marker nearer the Plateau.

events.name: The Torch: It Goes Out
events.intro: It goes out.

success.text: A very old man relights it from a lantern he's been carrying for this exact purpose. "Every year. Somebody drops it every year. I've stopped saying."

events.name: The Boulder Hall: Room 1
events.intro: Both boulders, both plates: a second door. Whoever does the pushing enjoys it more than it should.

success.text: A second door, and behind it a Star Piece someone hid and forgot.
An extra move per boulder. A second door, and a Star Piece.

events.name: The Boulder Hall: Room 2
events.intro: Dropped through the hole, then pushed again downstairs.

success.text: Downstairs, behind where it was, a TM: Earthquake.
Slowly. Downstairs, a TM: Earthquake.

events.name: The Boulder Hall: Room 3
events.intro: All three, in the order the scratches on the floor show.

success.text: A side door. A ledge. A nest of scorched stones, big enough to lie down in. One feather in it, still warm. A Moltres Sighting.
Three boulders, slowly. The nest, and one warm feather.

events.name: The Village at the Gate

remembers.notice: AJ is on a bench with his board. It says 98 WINS, and something else under it.
Giselle, with her blister, delighted about it.

events.intro: Outside the great gate, a fair that never quite packs up. Souvenir stalls, a noodle cart, a badge painter, a little stage where a Jigglypuff sometimes sings, benches of trainers comparing routes, and a board. On the benches, people this run has met.

success.text: A full rest. The cook's got eight flavours, one for each Badge; he gives you the one for the stage you found hardest. He's right.
He paints your eight on the back of your jacket. He paints a ninth circle, empty. "For the next one. There's always a next one."
Cork, by the gate. Hundreds of things pinned to it. A ribbon. A ticket. Half a fossil. A photograph of three stars in a daytime sky. A drawing of a Pidgey with the ears wrong.
The great gate.
